speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, frequent falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To determine the cause of these symptoms, can you tell me if these issues started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Circulation Stroke (likely Vertebrobasilar Insufficiency) with early signs of posterior cortical atrophy or frontal lobe dysfunction, given the sudden onset of right leg weakness, ataxia, falls, and concurrent cognitive/behavioral changes in a 44-year-old male. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain (DWI/FLAIR sequences).
